name: – Marcos Ros Sempere – After § 33 – Am 5
title: REPORT on a new strategy for media literacy and digital learning
part_text: 33a. Recalls that education falls within the competence of the Member States in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity enshrined in Article 165 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and that the Commission has no legislative authority over school curriculums; recalls that the role of schools is to impart knowledge, whereas fostering critical thinking is first and foremost the responsibility of parents; therefore opposes any attempt by the EU to impose educational content through recommendations, funding, or legislation; emphasises the risk that media literacy programmes funded by the Commission, under the guise of combating disinformation, could be used to standardise diverse media content and discredit sources of information critical of the EU; calls on the Member States, therefore, to retain full control over media literacy education, from design to implementation, while fully respecting the plurality of opinions and freedom of expression;
